Installation guide: OpenProject on Docker all-in-one container. It includes intro Docker prerequisite, supported architectures, limitations, available containers, verifying integrity, installation overview (two ways, single container guide), Quick Start command, explanation env vars, default admin password, stop CTRL-C, background -d, note pseudo-TTY. Production: persistent data directory command, stop/start/rm, configuration links, disabling HTTPS/HSTS, reverse proxy Apache/nginx examples root and subdirectory, plugins custom image, self-signed cert import, offline/air-gapped, Docker Swarm. 

We need rate each criterion.

Completeness: coverage of info needed to install, configure where required, verify software. It covers prerequisites (Docker Engine), architectures, quick start, production persistence, configuration (some, external advanced config), reverse proxy, HTTPS, HSTS, plugins, certs, offline, swarm. Verification: image integrity verification (cosign, scout), expected startup success message, default admin login, access URL, service ls output for swarm. But it is focused on all-in-one container; for recommended compose it redirects. Does it cover configuration enough? It points to advanced configuration; covers key env vars. Missing perhaps system requirements (RAM, disk), ports, backup/restore? Verify software maybe admin password. It is fairly complete for all-in-one. Could be 4 or 5. Need likely 4? It covers a lot, but maybe not all needed: no explicit verification that container running besides success message; no health endpoint; no troubleshooting except notes. But criteria asks installation, configure where required, verify. Good coverage. I'd give 4: comprehensive but relies on external advanced config and recommended method not included.

Structure: arranged to find and follow order. Headings clear: supported, limitations, containers, verify, overview, all-in-one quick start, production, config, reverse proxy, plugins, certs, offline, swarm. Good logical progression, but some sections out of order? Image integrity before installation perhaps optional. Overview says single container then quick start. Reverse proxy under production. It is easy to navigate. Could be 5? It has many subsections, clear. But maybe all-in-one title but includes compose/helm links; image verification is extensive. Still structure is good. I'd give 4 or 5. Since user asks find what needed and follow required order: yes. Maybe 5: well-organized with headings, quick start first, production later, advanced sections. However there are some cross-links and optional sections; not perfect. 4? We need calibrate. If 5 excellent: no issues? It has "OpenProject on Docker all-in-one container" but quick start uses all-in-one? yes. It includes verification section before installation, which could be optional but not disruptive. It has "Installation overview" after image integrity, which might delay quick start. But okay. I'd rate 4: generally logical, some advanced/optional content before quick start and external links for recommended method.

Clarity: instructions, commands, prerequisites, configuration values, expected outcomes precise and unambiguous. Commands mostly clear. Some ambiguity: quick start uses <your-secret-key-base> placeholder, explained. default admin password admin? It says success message indicating default administration password (login admin, password admin). Could be insecure but clear. Reverse proxy configs have typo? Apache SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/crt//server.key double slash. It says certificate and key located under /etc/ssl/crt/server.{crt, key} (syntax odd). In swarm, service list shows postgres:10 after postgres:13 inconsistency. Some commands inconsistent file names: offline save openproject-stable.tar.gz then gunzip openproject-12.tar.gz. This is an ambiguity/error. Plugins Dockerfile comment "RUN npm add npm <package-name>*" odd. But overall commands precise. Some placeholders «...» for S3. Could be 4? Due to minor inconsistencies and some assumptions. Maybe 3? Let's evaluate. It states expected outcomes (success message, access URL, service ls). It explains env vars. But errors: "There are two ways to run OpenProject. We'll cover each configuration in a separate of the following sections." missing "one". Minor. "server.{crt, key}" not proper brace expansion? It means crt and key. "SLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/crt//server.key" double slash. Offline filename mismatch: creates openproject-stable.tar.gz, later gunzip openproject-12.tar.gz. That could confuse. Also swarm service list inconsistency postgres:10 vs postgres:13. These are clarity issues. But not major for basic install. I'd score 3? The basic quick start is clear. For all guide, some inconsistencies. Criterion asks instructions, commands, prerequisites, configuration values, expected outcomes stated precisely and without ambiguity. The presence of contradictory file names and version inconsistencies reduces. But most are clear. Maybe 3 (adequate) or 4 (good). Need choose. If we want fair: 3 because of several inconsistencies in commands/config snippets that could cause ambiguity/errors. But basic installation commands are very clear. The guide is long; errors are minor. I'd lean 3 for clarity? Let's consider scale: 3 adequate: meets needs with some ambiguity or minor issues. Yes.

Understandability: easy to understand steps? Explains terms? It assumes Docker knowledge: docker run flags, ports, env vars, proxy, reverse proxy, swarm, cosign, SBOM/VEX. It explains some env vars and commands but not all technical terms (e.g., secret key base partially, pseudo-TTY, HSTS somewhat, attestation, cosign, OIDC). It provides links. For novice Docker user, may need prior knowledge. But step-by-step with explanations. Rate 3 or 4? It explains quick start values, but advanced sections use jargon without much explanation: "attestations", "predicate type", "keyless OIDC", "HSTS", "NFS", "S3", "fog". It assumes familiarity. It also tells to use external web server but not how to fully configure TLS beyond examples. It is understandable for intermediate/advanced DevOps. Criterion: consider whether guide explained technical terms or required know beforehand. It requires Docker knowledge; some terms not explained. I'd give 3: adequate, understandable for users with Docker/web server experience; not for beginners due to unexplained jargon. Could be 4 because explanations of environment variables and notes help. But "understandability" asks easy to understand installation/setup steps. Basic steps are easy. However overall guide has advanced concepts. Maybe 3.
